Starting: build the water solid in build123d, in metres, and check its volume against a hand-computed value (shell 3020 mm³ + three cylinder-outside-sphere lobes 17709 mm³ ≈ 20729 mm³).

```python
import os, subprocess, numpy as np
from build123d import *

CUBE = 0.040          # cube edge [m]
R_HOLLOW = 0.016      # spherical hollow radius
R_BALL   = 0.015      # ball radius
R_HOLE   = 0.012      # face hole radius

hollow = Sphere(R_HOLLOW)
ball   = Sphere(R_BALL)
cyl_z  = Cylinder(R_HOLE, CUBE)                      # axis z, -20..+20 mm
cyl_x  = Rot(0, 90, 0) * Cylinder(R_HOLE, CUBE)
cyl_y  = Rot(90, 0, 0) * Cylinder(R_HOLE, CUBE)

water = (hollow + cyl_x + cyl_y + cyl_z) - ball
print("volume [mm^3]", water.volume*1e9, " expected ~20729")
print("bbox [mm]", [round(v*1000,3) for v in water.bounding_box().min], [round(v*1000,3) for v in water.bounding_box().max])
print("faces", len(water.faces()), "solids", len(water.solids()))
```

Solid is one piece, volume matches the hand estimate (the 70 mm³ deficit is the x–y cylinder mutual overlap outside the sphere, which I double-counted). Now classify the 21 faces analytically so patches are named from surface identity, not bounding-box position.

Faces classify cleanly by surface identity: 8 spherical patches at |p|=16 mm (the hollow wall survives only as 8 octant slivers, because the six 12 mm holes overlap each other on the 16 mm sphere), 1 sphere at 15 mm (ball), 6 cylinders, 6 planes. I classify by the surface's own radius/axis, then export one STL per named group.
Areas confirm: ball 2827.4 = 4π·15², each opening 452.4 = π·12². Now write the STEP for gmsh and look at the shape — half-clipped so the 1 mm shell is visible.
Clip emptied some patches (e.g. the y− opening lies wholly on the removed side); skip empties.
`pv` was bound only in the cell that errored, so I re-emit the render self-contained.
Screenshot written but not shown; display it.

Shape reads correctly (red ball inside, green hole bores). Now import the STEP into gmsh and classify its surfaces by area + centre of mass, which are unambiguous here (ball 2827.4, hole wall 665.7, opening 452.4, hollow sliver 17.0 mm²).
Classification rule is clear. Set physical groups, a distance-based size field refining the 1 mm shell, and generate a coarse mesh first (0.5 mm in the gap, 2 mm elsewhere).
Convert to OpenFOAM. Need a minimal case skeleton for the utilities first.
Mesh OK; all 38368 boundary faces are in the 14 named patches (the `".*"` row is the group sum, defaultFaces is empty). Now measure the geometry from the mesh nodes themselves.
All named dimensions exact. Refine so the 1 mm shell gets ~3 cells across (0.30 mm) and regenerate.
Mesh OK. Verify the shell is actually resolved (cell size in the gap) and take a final look at a clipped section.

Built and meshed the water volume of the flooded ball cage, in metres.

**Geometry** (build123d, algebra mode): water = (sphere R=16 mm ∪ three through-cylinders R=12 mm on the x, y, z axes, spanning the 40 mm cube) − ball R=15 mm. One solid, volume 20658.6 mm³ against a hand check of ~20729 mm³ (the 70 mm³ difference is the mutual overlap of neighbouring bores outside the hollow, which the hand estimate double-counts).

**Measured against the request** (all from the mesh nodes, not the input numbers): ball radius 15.0000 mm; hollow wall radius 16.0000 mm; shell gap 1.0000 mm; bore radius 12.0000 mm on all six holes, each running from |axis| = 10.583 mm (= √(16²−12²), i.e. exactly where the bore meets the hollow) out to 20.000 mm; six openings planar at |coord| = 20.0000 mm with outer radius 12.0000 mm. Cube bbox (−20,−20,−20)…(20,20,20) mm.

**Patches**, named on the faces from their own surface identity (radius/axis/normal, never bbox position), one STL each in `constant/triSurface`: `ball`, `hollow`, `hole_xp/xm/yp/ym/zp/zm`, `opening_xp/xm/yp/ym/zp/zm` — 14 files, written before meshing. Note a consequence of the given dimensions: six R=12 mm holes on an R=16 mm sphere overlap one another, so the `hollow` patch survives only as eight slivers near the body diagonals, 135.7 mm² total; that is what the stated geometry gives, not a defect.

**Mesh**: gmsh tets on the STEP, size field 0.30 mm near ball/hollow growing to 1.5 mm, → 900 157 cells, converted with `gmshToFoam`. `checkMesh`: Mesh OK, 1 region, max non-orthogonality 69.5 (avg 21.1), max skewness 0.948, max aspect ratio 8.6, volume 2.0631e-5 m³ (0.13 % below the CAD volume, faceting). The 1 mm shell carries ~3.4 cells across (523 700 cells lie in it).

**Not checked**: the mesh is all-tet with no boundary layers; `gmshToFoam` also left a `water` cellZone/cellSet and gives every patch type `patch` (including walls) — patch *types* are boundary-condition work and I left them alone. Rendering is surface-only (EGL unavailable, OSMesa software path), so I verified the interior numerically rather than by a cut-plane picture of the cells.
